STANCE 41 - Instrument the decision point, not the trajectory: without a per-call counterfactual logit trace the intervention is unfalsifiable.

Mechanism. A redundant call is emitted at one specific decode step where the policy assigned more mass to a tool-call token than to an answer token. Everything upstream (prompt, prior observations, trajectory length) acts only through that margin. If the margin is never logged, every downstream claim about why redundancy fell is a story fitted to an aggregate. Logging the top-k logits and the answer-branch margin at each call site turns the defect into a measurable scalar with a boundary condition: interventions that do not move the margin cannot have fixed the cause, even if the rate moved.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: redundant calls concentrate at small answer-branch margins, with at least 70% of them below the median margin of legitimate calls. Falsified if the margin distributions of redundant and legitimate calls overlap with AUC below 0.6, which would mean the defect is not a marginal-decision phenomenon and no threshold or decode-time fix can separate the two classes.

Metrics. Per call site: answer-branch margin, top-k tool-call mass, temperature, trajectory token length, and adjudicated redundancy label. Aggregate: unnecessary-call rate (UCR), margin-separation AUC, and stratified accuracy on the tool-required stratum as the carried invariant. Guardrail: logging overhead in added p95 latency, since a trace that changes serving behavior contaminates its own measurement.

Controlled experiment. Enable logit-trace logging on a frozen checkpoint and replay a fixed logged window twice with identical seeds and decode config, once with tracing and once without, to confirm tracing is behaviorally inert. Then adjudicate a stratified sample of call sites and fit the margin-separation AUC. The manipulated variable is only instrumentation, so any behavioral delta between arms is a bug in the instrumentation, not a finding.

Confounders. Temperature and sampler settings rescale margins, so arms with different decode configs are not comparable. Adjudication of redundancy is itself a labeler with error, and label noise deflates AUC toward 0.5, which can masquerade as the falsification condition. Prefix caching alters timing and can shift which sites are sampled if sampling is time-based rather than trajectory-based.

Evidence and rollback. Report margin distributions, AUC, UCR and stratified accuracy as MEASURED with eval-set id, checkpoint hash, sampler config and labeler code version. The 70% concentration and 0.6 AUC bands are ESTIMATE, pre-registered before adjudication as the smallest separation that would justify a decode-time gate over a training-side fix. Roll back tracing if it adds more than 5% to p95 latency (ESTIMATE budget), and never report instrumentation coverage as a capability improvement.
risks: Logit tracing can perturb serving latency and contaminate the very window it measures.
Redundancy adjudication error deflates margin-separation AUC and can be misread as falsification.
evidence_required: Answer-branch margin distributions for adjudicated redundant versus legitimate calls, with separation AUC.
Tracing-on versus tracing-off replay showing behavioral inertness, plus added p95 latency from logging.

corrected_answer:
STANCE 42 - Contrarian: most 'redundant' calls are correct behavior under an unstated staleness policy; fix the specification before the model.

Mechanism. Redundancy is defined relative to an assumption that a prior result is still valid. For a pure calculator that assumption holds trivially, but agents share one policy across pure and impure tools, and nothing in the prompt or tool schema tells the model which results are cacheable. Absent a declared staleness contract, re-calling is a defensible conservative default. The mechanism of the fix is therefore specification: annotate each tool as pure or time-varying with an explicit validity window, so reuse becomes licensed rather than guessed.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: after adding purity and validity-window annotations to tool schemas, UCR on pure tools drops by at least 35% relative while UCR on time-varying tools stays flat within 5% relative. Falsified if both drop together, which would show the model is responding to prompt salience rather than to the semantic annotation, and the fix is a placebo.

Metrics. UCR split by tool purity class, reuse-of-stale-result rate on time-varying tools (the safety-critical inverse error), accuracy by stratum, calls per task at p50 and p95, and schema-annotation coverage. Guardrail: incorrect reuse of an expired result, which is a correctness fault far more expensive than a wasted call.

Controlled experiment. Two arms behind identical routing on one frozen checkpoint: unannotated schemas and annotated schemas, with a third placebo arm carrying length-matched but semantically empty annotations. Traffic split by hash of task id for stable balanced assignment. Weights are unchanged in all arms, isolating the schema contract as the only manipulated variable.

Confounders. Annotations lengthen the tool preamble and interact with context-length effects, which the placebo arm exists to absorb. The purity classification is human-authored and may be wrong for tools with hidden side effects. Traffic mix determines the pure-versus-impure ratio, so an aggregate UCR delta can be driven entirely by mix shift rather than behavior.

Evidence and rollback. Report per-class UCR, stale-reuse rate and stratified accuracy as MEASURED, naming the eval-set id, checkpoint hash and schema version. The 35% and 5% bands are ESTIMATE, fixed in advance as the pattern that would distinguish semantic response from salience response. Roll back annotations immediately if stale-reuse on time-varying tools exceeds 0.5% absolute (ESTIMATE gate); trading a cheap redundant call for a silently wrong cached answer is a strictly worse operating point.
risks: Purity annotations may be wrong for tools with hidden side effects, licensing unsafe reuse.
Reusing an expired result on a time-varying tool is a correctness fault worse than a redundant call.
evidence_required: UCR split by tool purity class across unannotated, annotated and length-matched placebo arms.
Stale-result reuse rate on time-varying tools with schema version and eval-set id recorded.

corrected_answer:
STANCE 43 - Separate the two populations first: an agent that cannot tell 'I computed this' from 'I recall this' needs a memory probe, not a policy patch.

Mechanism. The claim 'the answer is already known' bundles two distinct states: the value appears verbatim in the prefix, or the value is derivable from the prefix by arithmetic the model can do internally. These have different fixes. Verbatim-present redundancy is a retrieval failure and yields to context engineering; derivable-only redundancy is a computation-confidence failure and yields only to training or to an explicit scratchpad. Treating them as one population guarantees that any single intervention shows a diluted effect and gets misread as weak.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: the two populations respond differently, with a context-engineering intervention cutting verbatim-present redundancy by at least 40% relative while moving derivable-only redundancy by under 10% relative. Falsified if both classes move together within 10 points of each other, which would mean the split has no mechanistic content and a single scalar intervention is adequate.

Metrics. UCR decomposed into verbatim-present and derivable-only strata, stratum prevalence, per-stratum accuracy, calls per task by stratum, and inter-labeler agreement on the stratum assignment. Guardrail: the fraction of calls that cannot be assigned to either stratum, since a large unassignable mass invalidates the decomposition.

Controlled experiment. Adjudicate a stratified sample of call sites into the two classes with two independent labelers and a tie-break, then replay the same logged window on a frozen checkpoint under the context-engineering arm and the control arm, analyzing per stratum with assignment fixed before the arms are run. Fixing assignment beforehand prevents the intervention from redefining its own denominator.

Confounders. Derivability is a property of the model, not the transcript, so the label depends on which checkpoint is judging. Labeler disagreement is concentrated exactly on the boundary cases that drive the contrast. A context intervention that shortens prefixes can convert derivable-only cases into verbatim-present ones mid-experiment, breaking the fixed assignment if labels are recomputed.

Evidence and rollback. Report per-stratum UCR, prevalence, agreement statistics and unassignable fraction as MEASURED with eval-set id, checkpoint hash and labeler versions. The 40% and 10% thresholds are ESTIMATE, pre-registered as the divergence that would justify maintaining two separate remediation tracks. Abandon the decomposition if unassignable calls exceed 15% absolute (ESTIMATE gate), and report the split as an analysis artifact, never as evidence of model capability.
risks: Derivability labels depend on the judging checkpoint, so the stratum split is not checkpoint-portable.
A large unassignable fraction silently invalidates the two-population decomposition.
evidence_required: Per-stratum UCR and prevalence with assignment fixed before arms ran, plus inter-labeler agreement.
Unassignable-call fraction and per-stratum accuracy under both context-engineering and control arms.

STANCE 44 - Make the cost visible in the loop: charge the agent for calls in its own observation stream and measure whether visible price changes behavior.

Mechanism. The policy receives no signal that a call costs anything. Returning a running cost ledger as part of each tool observation converts an externality into in-context state the model can condition on. The mechanism is purely informational, and its boundary condition is that the model must be able to compare a running total against a stated budget, which is a two-integer comparison well within capability. Unlike a hard cap, this preserves the model's ability to spend when spending is warranted.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: exposing a running call-cost ledger reduces mean calls per task by at least 20% relative with no accuracy regression beyond 1 point on the tool-required stratum. Falsified if calls per task moves under 5% relative, which would show the policy does not condition on numeric budget state and only hard admission control will bound the tail.

Metrics. Mean and p95 calls per task, UCR, accuracy by stratum, GPU-seconds per completed task, and budget-overrun rate. Guardrail: premature abandonment, meaning tasks that end without an answer while the stated budget was not exhausted, which indicates the ledger induced excess caution.

Controlled experiment. Three arms on a frozen checkpoint and fixed eval set: no ledger, accurate ledger, and a scrambled-ledger placebo that shows numbers uncorrelated with actual spend. The placebo distinguishes response to the semantic content of the budget from response to the mere presence of extra numeric tokens in the observation.

Confounders. Ledger text lengthens every observation and compounds over a trajectory, interacting with context-length effects. Cost accounting itself may be wrong if some calls are cached at the serving layer, so the displayed price can diverge from real GPU-seconds. Task difficulty mix determines how much legitimate spend is required, so a mix shift can mimic or mask the effect.

Evidence and rollback. Report calls-per-task histograms, UCR, stratified accuracy, GPU-seconds per completed task and abandonment rate as MEASURED per arm with eval-set id, checkpoint hash and ledger version. The 20% and 5% bands are ESTIMATE, pre-declared as the effect size justifying a change to every tool response format. Roll back if premature abandonment exceeds 1.5% absolute (ESTIMATE gate); a ledger is a serving-side control and any savings must be reported as system efficiency, not as model capability.
risks: A visible cost ledger can induce premature abandonment of tasks that still had budget.
Displayed prices diverge from real GPU-seconds when calls are cached at the serving layer.
evidence_required: Calls-per-task histograms and UCR across no-ledger, accurate-ledger and scrambled-ledger placebo arms.
Premature-abandonment rate and GPU-seconds per completed task with ledger version recorded.

corrected_answer:
STANCE 45 - Guard the training fix with a capability invariant: any reward against redundancy must be shown not to teach under-calling.

Mechanism. Penalizing extra calls in a preference or RL objective creates a gradient toward calling less, and the objective cannot distinguish a redundant call from a necessary one unless the reward is conditioned on necessity. The predictable failure mode is that the model learns the cheap policy of answering from parametric memory, which lowers UCR and simultaneously lowers accuracy on exactly the tasks where tools matter. The mechanism of a safe fix is therefore an asymmetric reward: penalize only calls adjudicated redundant, and carry accuracy on the tool-required stratum as a hard invariant.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: an asymmetric, necessity-conditioned penalty reduces UCR by at least 30% relative while tool-required-stratum accuracy stays within 1 point of the pre-training baseline. Falsified if accuracy drops by more than 2 points at any UCR reduction, which would establish that the reward cannot separate necessity from redundancy at the available label quality and the training path should be abandoned.

Metrics. UCR, tool-required-stratum accuracy, under-calling rate (tasks that needed a tool and used none), calls per task at p50 and p95, and reward-model or adjudicator precision and recall against held-out human labels. Guardrail: under-calling rate, which is the direct signature of the failure mode this stance exists to prevent.

Controlled experiment. Train two arms from the identical base checkpoint with identical data, seed, and optimizer state: one with a symmetric per-call penalty and one with the necessity-conditioned asymmetric penalty, plus the untrained base as control. Evaluate all three on the same frozen eval set with matched decode config, so the only manipulated variable is the reward shape.

Confounders. Adjudicator error propagates directly into the reward and is the dominant confounder; low-precision necessity labels make the asymmetric arm behave like the symmetric one. Training-set composition determines how often necessity is even at stake. Improvements measured on the same distribution used to fit the adjudicator will not generalize and must be checked on a held-out task family.

Evidence and rollback. Report UCR, stratified accuracy, under-calling rate and adjudicator precision/recall as MEASURED with training-run id, base checkpoint hash, data snapshot and eval-set id. The 30% target and 1-to-2 point accuracy bands are ESTIMATE, registered before training as the acceptance and abort criteria. Revert to the base checkpoint if the under-calling rate rises by more than 1 point absolute (ESTIMATE gate), and keep the base weights and a tested rollback path live for the full evaluation window.
risks: A symmetric call penalty teaches under-calling, lowering UCR while degrading tool-required accuracy.
Necessity-label error propagates directly into the reward and collapses the asymmetric arm into the symmetric one.
evidence_required: UCR, tool-required-stratum accuracy and under-calling rate for symmetric, asymmetric and base-checkpoint arms.
Adjudicator precision and recall against held-out human labels, plus training-run id and data snapshot hash.

corrected_answer:
STANCE 46 - Test transfer before shipping: a fix validated only on the calculator is a fix to one tool schema, not to the redundancy behavior.

Mechanism. The calculator is the easiest possible case: pure, cheap, deterministic, and with short results. Any intervention tuned on it can exploit those properties, for example by keying reuse on short numeric observations, and then fail on retrieval, code execution, or cluster-query tools whose results are long, partially stale, or non-deterministic. The mechanism of a credible claim is held-out tool families: the intervention must be developed on one family and evaluated, unmodified, on families it never saw.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: an intervention developed on the calculator retains at least 60% of its relative UCR reduction on held-out tool families. Falsified if retained effect is under 25% relative, which would classify the intervention as tool-specific tuning and forbid describing it as a general redundancy fix.

Metrics. UCR per tool family on development and held-out families, retained-effect ratio, accuracy per family, calls per task per family, and family prevalence in the eval mix. Guardrail: any family where UCR increases, which indicates the intervention is actively harmful outside its development distribution.

Controlled experiment. Freeze the intervention configuration after development on the calculator family with no further tuning, then run it against a held-out eval set covering retrieval, code-execution and cluster-query tools, alongside the unintervened control on the same set. Configuration freeze before the held-out run is what makes the transfer estimate honest rather than a second fitting pass.

Confounders. Family prevalence differences make aggregate UCR move without any per-family change, so all reporting must be per family. Held-out families differ in baseline difficulty, so a low retained effect can reflect a harder baseline rather than poor transfer. Any post-hoc reconfiguration silently converts the held-out set into a development set and invalidates the entire claim.

Evidence and rollback. Report per-family UCR, retained-effect ratio and per-family accuracy as MEASURED with the frozen configuration hash, eval-set ids, and checkpoint hash, plus an explicit statement of which families were development and which were held out. The 60% and 25% retention bands are ESTIMATE, pre-registered as ship and no-ship criteria. Block rollout to any family whose UCR regresses at all, and describe the result as serving-behavior transfer, never as a model domain-capability gain.
risks: An intervention tuned on the calculator can exploit short pure numeric results and fail on other tool families.
Any post-hoc reconfiguration turns the held-out set into a development set and voids the transfer claim.
evidence_required: Per-tool-family UCR and accuracy on development and held-out families with the configuration frozen before the held-out run.
Retained-effect ratio per family and an explicit list of which families were development versus held out.

STANCE 47 - Route by decision confidence rather than by task: a cheap classifier at the call site can gate the expensive path.

Mechanism. If redundant calls concentrate at low answer-branch margins, a small classifier over cheap features (margin, distance to the last matching observation, tool purity class, trajectory length) can predict redundancy before the call is dispatched and suppress it, substituting the prior observation. The mechanism is admission control conditioned on a learned score rather than a fixed cap, which preserves legitimate deep call chains. The boundary condition is classifier precision: at the operating point, a false suppression removes a call the task genuinely needed.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: a classifier reaches precision at or above 0.9 at recall 0.5 for redundant calls on held-out trajectories. Falsified if no operating point achieves precision 0.8 at recall 0.3, which would mean cheap features do not carry enough signal and gating must not be deployed at any threshold.

Metrics. Classifier precision, recall and calibration on held-out trajectories, post-gating UCR, accuracy on the tool-required stratum, false-suppression rate, and added p95 latency from scoring. Guardrail: false-suppression rate, the operationally dangerous error, tracked separately from aggregate accuracy because it can be masked by easy tasks.

Controlled experiment. Fit the classifier on trajectories from one time window and evaluate on a strictly later disjoint window, then run a shadow deployment where the gate scores and logs decisions without suppressing anything, followed by a small-percentage enforced arm. Shadow mode measures precision at the real operating distribution without exposing traffic to false suppressions.

Confounders. Label quality bounds measurable precision, so an apparently mediocre classifier may be adjudicator-limited. Distribution shift between fitting and enforcement windows degrades the operating point silently. Enforcement changes the trajectories that generate future training data, creating a feedback loop that makes offline precision estimates stale.

Evidence and rollback. Report precision-recall curves, calibration, post-gating UCR, stratified accuracy and false-suppression rate as MEASURED with the fitting-window id, evaluation-window id, classifier version and checkpoint hash. The 0.9 at 0.5 target and 0.8 at 0.3 abort thresholds are ESTIMATE, set before fitting. Disable the gate automatically if false suppression exceeds 1% absolute (ESTIMATE gate) or if tool-required accuracy drops more than 1 point, and keep shadow mode as the permanent fallback configuration.
risks: False suppression removes a call the task genuinely needed and is masked by aggregate accuracy.
Enforcement reshapes future trajectories, making offline precision estimates stale via feedback.
evidence_required: Precision-recall curve and calibration on a strictly later disjoint trajectory window.
Shadow-mode false-suppression estimate and post-gating stratified accuracy with classifier version recorded.

STANCE 48 - Account for the serving topology: in a disaggregated deployment, a redundant call is a KV-cache and scheduler event, not just a token cost.

Mechanism. Each extra tool call ends a decode segment and forces a new prefill of the grown trajectory. Under prefill/decode disaggregation, this pushes load onto the prefill pool and generates a KV transfer to the decode pool over the interconnect. If the trajectory prefix is cached, the marginal prefill cost is small; if the cache missed because the observation changed the prefix tail, the cost is a full recompute. So the true price of redundancy is bimodal and determined by cache-hit behavior, which means a UCR reduction can produce anywhere from negligible to large capacity savings.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: prefill-pool GPU-seconds per completed task scale with UCR at a slope steeper than 0.5, meaning redundancy is a material capacity driver. Falsified if the slope is under 0.1, which would show prefix caching already absorbs nearly all redundant-call cost and the entire effort should be justified on latency or correctness grounds, not capacity.

Metrics. Prefill-pool GPU-seconds per completed task, trajectory prefix cache hit rate, KV transfer bytes and transfer p95 latency, decode-pool p95 inter-token latency, and UCR. Guardrail: end-to-end p95 task latency, since shifting work between pools can improve one pool's numbers while degrading user-visible latency.

Controlled experiment. Replay a fixed logged workload at several induced UCR levels (by varying an orchestrator gate threshold) against a frozen checkpoint on a fixed cluster topology with autoscaling pinned and pool sizes held constant. Pinning autoscaling is essential; otherwise the system compensates for load changes and the measured slope reflects the autoscaler, not the workload.

Confounders. Cache hit rate depends on request arrival order and tenancy, so replay order must be preserved. Interconnect contention from co-tenant traffic perturbs KV transfer latency independently of the manipulated variable. Batch composition changes with call rate, altering per-token efficiency in ways unrelated to redundancy.

Evidence and rollback. Report GPU-seconds per completed task, cache hit rate, KV transfer bytes and latency, and end-to-end p95 as MEASURED with the cluster topology description, pinned pool sizes, replay window id and checkpoint hash. The 0.5 and 0.1 slope bands are ESTIMATE, chosen before the sweep as the capacity-relevance decision boundary. Revert any gate threshold change that raises end-to-end p95 by more than 10% (ESTIMATE budget), and report all savings strictly as system-level capacity, not as model capability.
risks: Autoscaling left unpinned compensates for load changes and corrupts the capacity slope measurement.
Shifting work between prefill and decode pools can improve pool metrics while degrading end-to-end p95.
evidence_required: Prefill-pool GPU-seconds per completed task versus induced UCR level with autoscaling pinned and pool sizes fixed.
Prefix cache hit rate, KV transfer bytes and p95 transfer latency, plus end-to-end p95 task latency.

STANCE 49 - Pre-register the analysis or the result is not evidence: this defect is unusually easy to fix by accident and confirm by selection.

Mechanism. UCR is a constructed metric whose value depends on the redundancy definition, the eval mix, the labeler version and the replay window. Each of those is a researcher degree of freedom, and with four such knobs a null intervention can be shown positive by selecting the combination that looks best. Pre-registering the primary metric definition, the eval-set id, the labeler code version, the sample size and the number of interim looks removes those degrees of freedom before the data exist. The mechanism is procedural, and it is the only one that makes the other stances' numbers interpretable.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: pre-registered analyses of these interventions yield smaller effect sizes than post-hoc analyses of the same data, with a median shrinkage of at least 30% relative. Falsified if pre-registered and post-hoc effects agree within 10% relative across the intervention set, which would indicate the analysis flexibility in this pipeline is not actually being exploited.

Metrics. Pre-registered primary UCR difference with a confidence interval, all pre-declared secondary metrics reported regardless of outcome, realized versus planned sample size, interim-look count, and the shrinkage ratio between post-hoc and pre-registered estimates. Guardrail: any metric definition changed after data collection began, which must be reported as an amendment with its timestamp.

Controlled experiment. Register the analysis plan at a commit hash before running any arm, then execute the intervention arms and compute both the pre-registered analysis and an unconstrained post-hoc analysis on identical data. The manipulated variable is the analysis procedure alone, with data held fixed, which isolates analytic flexibility from any real effect.

Confounders. A pre-registration that is vague is not a constraint, so plan specificity must itself be assessed. Interim looks inflate false positives unless the stopping rule was registered. If the same team performs both analyses, knowledge of the post-hoc result contaminates judgment calls left open in the plan.

Evidence and rollback. Publish the plan commit hash, planned and realized sample sizes, interim-look count, the primary effect with its interval, and every secondary metric as MEASURED with eval-set id, checkpoint hash and labeler version. The 30% shrinkage expectation and 10% agreement band are ESTIMATE, declared in the plan itself. Treat any intervention whose support exists only in a post-hoc analysis as not shipped, and record process compliance as a research-hygiene property rather than as a model capability result.
risks: Four researcher degrees of freedom (definition, eval mix, labeler, window) allow a null result to be shown positive.
Unregistered interim looks inflate false-positive rate and vague plans provide no real constraint.
evidence_required: The analysis plan commit hash, planned versus realized sample size, and interim-look count.
Primary UCR difference with confidence interval and every pre-declared secondary metric reported in full.

STANCE 50 - Sequence the whole program as a staged gate: cheapest reversible fix first, weights last, with one carried invariant at every rung.

Mechanism. The candidate fixes differ by orders of magnitude in cost and reversibility: system-prompt wording, tool-schema annotation, observation formatting, orchestrator gating, then weight updates. Running them in cost order means each rung's effect is measured against a baseline that already includes every cheaper fix, so no expensive intervention is credited with a gain a one-line prompt change would have delivered. The boundary condition is that every rung must carry the same invariant, tool-required-stratum accuracy, or a rung can buy UCR reduction with silent capability loss.

Falsifiable hypothesis. H1: cumulative UCR reduction is dominated by the first two rungs, with prompt and schema changes together delivering at least 60% of the total reduction achieved by the full ladder. Falsified if the first two rungs deliver under 20%, which would justify going directly to gating and training and would mean under-specification was never the binding constraint.

Metrics. Per-rung marginal UCR reduction, cumulative UCR, tool-required-stratum accuracy at every rung, calls per task at p50 and p95, GPU-seconds per completed task, and revert time actually exercised per rung. Guardrail: the carried accuracy invariant, checked at every rung with a fixed abort band rather than at the end of the ladder.

Controlled experiment. Run rungs sequentially on a frozen checkpoint against a fixed eval set, holding all prior rungs in place and changing exactly one thing per rung, with a re-measured control arm at each stage to detect drift in the eval harness itself. Re-measuring the control at each rung is what separates true marginal effects from harness or traffic drift accumulating over the program.

Confounders. Sequential testing accumulates multiple-comparison risk and requires a pre-declared correction. Later rungs are evaluated on a baseline shaped by earlier ones, so marginal effects are order-dependent and not interchangeable. Eval-harness drift over a long program can manufacture apparent marginal gains, which is exactly what the re-measured control detects.

Evidence and rollback. Every rung gate must cite MEASURED numbers with eval-set id, checkpoint hash, labeler and gate code versions, plus an exercised revert record proving the rollback path works, not merely that it exists. The 60% and 20% attribution bands are ESTIMATE, pre-registered as the decision rule for whether to climb past the cheap rungs. Abort the ladder and revert to the last green rung if tool-required accuracy falls more than 1 point absolute (ESTIMATE gate); all reported gains are serving and orchestration behavior under a frozen policy and are not evidence of model domain capability.
risks: Sequential rungs accumulate multiple-comparison risk without a pre-declared correction.
Eval-harness drift over a long program manufactures apparent marginal gains at later rungs.
evidence_required: Per-rung marginal and cumulative UCR with a re-measured control arm at each stage to detect harness drift.
Tool-required-stratum accuracy at every rung plus an exercised revert record demonstrating each rollback path.
